overview: In the Van Geet 1.Nc3 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6, White strikes in the centre at once with 3.d4, often reaching a Scotch-like position after 3...exd4 4.Nxd4 with the extra Nc3. Black can also play 3...Bb4 or 3...exd4 and then ...Nf6, with a standard open game. I am not sure of the exact branches.

white_ideas.idea: Play 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 and aim for open lines with Bb5 or Nxc6
Develop with Bc4, Be3 and castle quickly
Use the early d4 to gain space and open the position

black_ideas.idea: Take on d4 and develop ...Nf6 and ...Bc5 or ...Bb4
Trade the d4 knight to relieve the cramp
Hit back at the centre with ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Scotch-like open centre after exd4 Nxd4
Open game with the e-pawn exchanged and pieces active

character.notes: Open centre with piece play but no immediate tactics; I read it as even.

gambit.notes: d4 is recaptured on d4 at once; no material changes hands.

soundness.notes: It is a sound Scotch-style set-up.

structure.notes: The centre opens early, as in the Scotch: open.

approach.notes: The Van Geet is a rare opening that strong players seldom pick; this is a branch of it. Offbeat, low confidence.

level.notes: Open game plans, with little to memorise.

character.reason: An open centre without forcing sharpness.

soundness.reason: A Scotch-like set-up with a sound structure.

structure.reason: The d-pawn is exchanged and the pieces get open lines.
